Works Cited

Azzara, Christopher D., and Richard F. Grunow. Developing Musicianship through Improvisation, Book 1: C Instruments. GIA Publications, 2006. Unit repertoire songs (melody and chords) transcribed into the dmti set of apps/tunes/tunes-object.js: “Mary Ann” (p. 17), “Joshua” (p. 33), “Down by the Riverside” (p. 69); “Long, Long Ago” (p. 1) and “Simple Gifts” (p. 51) were already in the collection. Part 2, Echo Tonal Patterns of Units 4 and 5 (solfège, p. xi), copied into dmti1-unit4-tonal / -unit5-tonal in apps/patterns/pattern-set.js with C as DO (Units 1–3 are the site’s major-I-V and minor-i-V); Echo Rhythm Patterns of Units 1–5 (pp. 2, 18, 34, 52, 71; syllables, pp. vii–ix), dmti1-unit1-rhythm … -unit5-rhythm in apps/rhythms/rhythm-pattern-object.js. Reproduced with permission.

Azzara, Christopher D., and Richard F. Grunow. Developing Musicianship through Improvisation, Book 2: C Instruments. GIA Publications, 2010. Unit repertoire songs (melody and chords) transcribed into the dmti set of apps/tunes/tunes-object.js: “When the Saints Go Marching In” (p. 1) and “Motherless Child” (p. 39); “Amazing Grace” was already in the collection. Part 2, Echo Tonal Patterns of Units 1–3 (solfège, p. ix; the lower of the two octaves printed), dmti2-unit1-tonal … -unit3-tonal in apps/patterns/pattern-set.js with C as DO (C as LA in Unit 3); Echo Rhythm Patterns of Units 1–3 (pp. 2, 22, 40; syllables, pp. vii–viii), dmti2-unit1-rhythm … -unit3-rhythm in apps/rhythms/rhythm-pattern-object.js. Reproduced with permission.

Azzara, Christopher D., and Richard F. Grunow. Developing Musicianship through Improvisation, Book 3: C Instruments. GIA Publications, 2010. Unit 1, “Saint Louis Blues”: the twelve Blue Note Patterns (pp. ix, 6), copied into the dmti-blue-notes set of apps/patterns/pattern-set.js with C as DO; the twelve Echo Tonal Patterns of the same page (p. 6, solfège p. ix) are dmti3-unit1-tonal, those of Unit 2 “Transformation” (p. x) dmti3-unit2-tonal and of Unit 3 “Red Wings” (p. xi) dmti3-unit3-tonal (lower octave where two are printed); the Echo Rhythm Patterns of the three units (syllables, pp. vii–viii) are dmti3-unit1-rhythm … -unit3-rhythm in apps/rhythms/rhythm-pattern-object.js. Unit repertoire tunes (melody and chords) transcribed into the dmti set of apps/tunes/tunes-object.js: “Transformation” (p. 23) and “Red Wings” (pp. 47–48), both by Azzara. Reproduced with permission.

Grunow, Richard F., Edwin E. Gordon, and Christopher D. Azzara. Jump Right In: The Instrumental Series. Teacher’s Guide for Recorder. Rev. ed., GIA Publications, 1999. 24 rote songs transcribed into the jri-recorder set of apps/tunes/tunes-object.js (melody and chords), from the piano-accompaniment pages (pp. 258–315). Tonal Patterns from Student Book Two (pp. 321–324; major, minor, Dorian and Mixolydian tonic, dominant and subdominant sets, the minor, Dorian and Mixolydian ones being the site’s 322a/b, 323a/b, 324a/b) and the Student Book One tonic and dominant lesson set (pp. 46–47), jri-recorder-tonal-* in apps/patterns/pattern-set.js with C as DO (or LA, RE, SO); Rhythm Patterns from Student Book Two (pp. 325–334), jri-recorder-rhythm-* in apps/rhythms/rhythm-pattern-object.js. Reproduced with permission.
